canonical_question: Is the 'brittle fractured grains' description in suction-assisted cast indicative of a different crystallographic cleavage plane compared to the gravity cast?

question_variants.question: Is the 'brittle fractured grains' description in suction-assisted cast indicative of a different crystallographic cleavage plane compared to the gravity cast?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text states that brittle fractured grains were seen in suction-assisted cast and that fracture is inter-crystalline, but it does not specify the crystallographic cleavage planes or compare them to gravity cast to determine if they differ.

answers.answer: The text mentions 'brittle fractured grains together with porous regions can be seen' in suction-assisted cast and 'The figures show that the fracture is inter-crystalline in both cases'. However, it does not identify specific crystallographic cleavage planes for either casting method.
answers.boundary_limitation: No crystallographic plane data provided to distinguish between casts
evidence_spans: Figure 1 a depicts a back-scattered SEM image of the gravity-cast material prior to HIP, while Figure 1 b shows the suction-assisted casting. Figure 1 c,d depict the back-scattered SEM images of these two castings after HIP. Note that both materials were single phased before undergoing HIP, while a darker phase is discernible inside the bright matrix after HIP.
XRD spectra of both the gravity and the suction-assisted cast samples before HIP (see Figure 2 a,b respectively) correspond to single-phase NbTaTi-based BCC material.

As ZrHf solid solution phase is comprised of HCP elements (at room temperature), it has an HCP structure and thus exhibits the characteristic X-ray diffraction pattern of other HCP phases. Contrary to the ZrHf, the NbTaTi solid solution phase is comprised of BCC elements and therefore has a characteristic X-ray diffraction pattern of other BCC-structured substances.

source_evidence_spans: in the case of the suction-assisted cast, brittle fractured grains together with porous regions can be seen.
